summary.title: 我负责一款人眼安全级别的 1550 nm 相干激光雷达（LiDAR）接收前端
summary.question: 我负责一款人眼安全级别的 1550 nm 相干激光雷达（LiDAR）接收前端的窄带滤波膜研发。接收机使用 1550 nm 附近的窄线宽激光，需要该波段尽可能高的透过率（目标 ≥ 0.95），同时大幅抑制 1400-1500 nm 和 1600-1700 nm 两个邻近波段的背景辐射，以减少阳光及其他杂散光的干扰。请在空气入射、熔融石英基底条件下，仅使用 Ta2O5 和 SiO2 设计一个平面多层介质膜，膜系总层数不超过 30 层。

problem.compatibility_reason: Request specifies planar isotropic layered media compatible with transfer-matrix method.
ambiguities: angle of incidence not explicitly specified
exact passband width around 1550 nm not defined

metrics.rationale: User states '1550 nm 附近的窄线宽激光，需要该波段尽可能高的透过率（目标 ≥ 0.95）' - maximize transmittance in the 1550 nm passband
User requests '大幅抑制 1400-1500 nm...背景辐射' - maximize reflectance (minimize transmission) in this stopband
User requests '大幅抑制...1600-1700 nm 两个邻近波段的背景辐射' - maximize reflectance (minimize transmission) in this second stopband

scoring.metric_rationale: Three metrics directly map to the user's three spectral requirements: (1) high transmittance at 1550 nm passband using mean_transmittance maximize over a 10 nm narrow band appropriate for '窄线宽激光', (2) suppression of 1400-1500 nm using reflectance_stopband maximize, (3) suppression of 1600-1700 nm using reflectance_stopband maximize. The 1545-1555 nm passband width accommodates '窄带滤波膜' while allowing practical filter design margin. Layer count constraint (≤30) is a design variable limit handled by the optimizer, not a ranking metric. Deliberately omitted: angle and polarization selectors since user did not specify them (defaults to normal incidence, unpolarized); absorption metrics since user focuses on transmittance/reflectance for background suppression.
scoring.formula_rationale: This arrangement treats the passband transmission and both stopband rejections as equally critical contributors to the filter's utility. The user's goal of 'highest possible transmittance' is served by adding the transmittance metric directly, while the requirement to 'significantly suppress' background radiation in both neighboring bands is served by adding their reflectance metrics, where higher reflectance equals better suppression. Equal coefficients are used because the request imposes no hierarchy between the signal band and the noise bands, nor between the two noise bands, and all measurements share the same 0-to-1 scale.
